decisions.title: Skip unrecognized categories — don't throw
decisions.chose: Detect the out-of-union value and pass the record over.
decisions.rejected: Let it reach the exhaustive switch and throw, or widen the union to accept it
decisions.why: The upstream service emits categories outside our closed union; its generated client surfaces them as an unknown-enum sentinel that adapters cast in blindly. That value hit an exhaustive switch and threw — and since the handler logs-and-rethrows, it became a poison-message retry loop. The upstream team confirmed these records should be ignored.
decisions.quote: We confirmed with the upstream team that these records should be ignored / passed over.

decisions.title: Guard once in the shared business layer, not per adapter
decisions.chose: Put the check in OrderSubscription, which every adapter funnels through.
decisions.rejected: Validate in each adapter — queue handlers, the poller, the linked-record fetch
decisions.why: The unsafe cast happens in several adapters, but they all converge on the subscription before business logic runs. One choke point covers every entry point — created, updated, cancelled, fulfilled, refunded — instead of scattering the same validation and missing one.
decisions.quote: OrderSubscription — the single business layer all adapters funnel through — now skips records with an unrecognized category at every entry point.

decisions.title: Treat an unrecognized LINKED record as absent
decisions.chose: Behave as if there is no linked record.
decisions.rejected: Throw while building linked-record event properties
decisions.why: Enrichment reads the record's linked sibling. If that record carries a sentinel category, the same switch would throw mid-enrichment — turning an unprocessable neighbour into a failure of the current event. Treating it as absent degrades gracefully: the current event still ships.
decisions.quote: Treat a linked record with an unrecognized category as if there were none, rather than throwing while building its event properties.

decisions.title: Make every skip observable
decisions.chose: Warning log plus a new record_skipped_unrecognized_category metric.
decisions.why: A silent skip and a lost message look identical from outside — and this path exists because an upstream contract is leaking. The metric turns 'we're dropping records' into a rate the team can alarm on and hand back upstream. The skip is a symptom worth watching, not a fix to forget.
decisions.quote: Skips are observable: a warning log + a new record_skipped_unrecognized_category metric.

decisions.title: Leave the exhaustive switch as an unreachable invariant
decisions.rejected: Add a default arm to absorb unknown values
decisions.why: The upstream guard means the switch can no longer be reached with a bad value. Softening it with a default would silently absorb future real bugs; keeping it strict documents the invariant 'everything reaching here is recognized' and still throws loudly if a different path ever breaks that.
decisions.quote: The exhaustive switch in categoryLabel is left as-is (now an unreachable defensive invariant).
decisions.note: A deliberate non-change — invisible in the diff.

decisions.title: Count null as a recognized category
decisions.chose: Include null in the recognized set, so it processes normally.
decisions.rejected: Treat null as unrecognized and skip it too
decisions.why: null is a legitimate member of OrderCategory ('no specific category'), distinct from the sentinel string signalling an out-of-union value. Skipping null would drop valid records that simply have no category assigned.
decisions.inferNote: The code marks null as recognized with an inline comment, but the reasoning — that null is a valid domain value unlike the sentinel — is reconstructed from the type definition. The PR body doesn't discuss null, and the rejected alternative is illustrative.
